reference: POSIX ed command contracts independently specify append/print, BRE substitution, search/marks, read/write, undo, copy and join. GNU ed is unavailable in the reference environment, so these are literal contract checks, not GNU parity. Bash type/help cases cover metadata only.
coverage: Bash type and help metadata for the static ed builtin and its synopsis/documented command set.
Append, numbered range printing, and line-number output under -s.
Global basic-regular-expression substitution with the matched-text replacement character.
Forward and backward search address wraparound plus a named line mark.
Reading and writing relative fixture files, with their line contents verified by Bash builtins.
Undo of a substitution after a saved clean buffer.
Copying a range to the end, joining lines, printing the changed buffer, and writing the result.
Saved-file size checks include the final newline and reject trailing bytes.
exclusions: No GNU ed binary is available, so no case is represented as parity; no substitute implementation is used as an oracle.
Modified-buffer quit prompts and other terminal interaction require a future disposable PTY driver.
Binary/NUL-containing input, unusual filenames, malformed commands, and the full GNU ed option surface are outside this focused contract suite.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify ed as a builtin when PATH is empty.
The Bash help entry must expose the documented synopsis, command summary, and undo-history note.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ed)
[[ $doc == *'ed [-s] [FILE]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Small ed-style editor'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Undo history is capped at 1024 entries by default'* ]]
printf 'help metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: POSIX ed append plus n and = commands print line numbers and text in their specified forms.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
alpha
beta
.
1,2n
2=
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE substitution with g and replacement '&' must replace each match with the matched text surrounded by angle brackets.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
id=7 id=42
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: Forward and backward regular-expression addresses wrap through the buffer, and a marked line remains addressable.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
red
.
1ka
/blue/
?red?
'a
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The r command inserts a relative file after the current line; verify the resulting buffer text.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > payload.txt
ed -s <<'ED'
a
head
.
r payload.txt
1,$p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The w command creates a relative fixture file from the buffer; read it back with Bash builtins to verify bytes as lines.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
north
south
.
w saved.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < saved.txt
[[ $(<saved.txt) == $'north\nsouth' && $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s saved.txt) == 12 ]]

cases.purpose: Undo restores the line before the most recent substitution; the saved clean state also permits a normal quit.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
before
.
w saved.txt
s/before/after/
u
1p
q
ED

cases.purpose: The t command copies an addressed range after the destination, j joins addressed lines without a separator, and w persists the final buffer.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
green
.
1,2t$
1,$p
4,5j
1,$p
w final.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf 'file:%s\n' "$line"; done < final.txt
[[ $(<final.txt) == $'red\nblue\ngreen\nredblue' && $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s final.txt) == 23 ]]
cases.stdout:
red
blue
green
red
blue
red
blue
green
redblue
file:red
file:blue
file:green
file:redblue

cases.purpose: Check the editor's modified-buffer quit warning and response while attached to a terminal.
POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
xx1 y22 z333
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "xx<1> y<22> z<333>" ]]

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
abc
.
1s/^/X/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "Xabc" ]]
